correctness.rationale: The side invariant is forced by forbidden coordinates. Canonical representatives realize all 2^k signatures because endpoints cannot lie on the disallowed sides. A complete swap-case analysis proves feasibility of bubble sorting to the canonical representative, bounded by binomial(n,2). An independent Python BFS/normalization checker exhaustively checks all masks for n=2..7, while independently implemented C++ DSU checks all masks for n=2..8. Finite tests corroborate but are not used to extrapolate the general result.

evidence: An allowed permutation is a perfect matching in the bipartite graph K_{n,n} with selected diagonal edges deleted; exchanging consecutive positions switches matching partners on adjacent indexed left vertices.
It is also the induced subgraph on feasible permutations in the ordinary permutahedron.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: These equivalent models were compared by transition restrictions, not merely by graph names; full crown-graph matching switches can involve nonconsecutive positions, so their known connectivity does not cover this claim.

value.rationale: This all-parameter theorem determines the exact exponential number of components, an explicit complete component invariant and short canonical paths for an arbitrary subset of diagonal constraints. It resolves a natural obstruction in adjacency-preserving derangement generation, which cannot be inferred from Gray codes permitting arbitrary transpositions. Component sizes, exact diameters, and general forbidden-board patterns remain open.
